Laura / team —

Below is a legally defensible, commercially pragmatic approach we can take. I recommend we offer the buyer a choice with our preferred anchor listed first. Short version for procurement: "Liability is limited to the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (b) $250,000; insurance recoveries will reduce Redwood's liability to the extent actually collected net of the customer's deductible." Rationale: the annualized fee anchor ties exposure to recent usage and is easier for both sides to forecast; a modest dollar floor prevents immaterial disputes when fees are minimal.

Draft language (two bullets we can drop into the MSA):
- Limitation: Except for liability arising from (i) willful misconduct; (ii) gross negligence causing data breach; (iii) intellectual property indemnity; Redwood's aggregate liability for direct damages shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood for the services in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (ii) $250,000.
- Insurance offset mechanics: If Customer receives insurance proceeds related to the same damages, Redwood's liability shall be reduced by the amount actually received by Customer from insurance, after reasonable deduction for Customer's deductible and any taxes or costs incurred to recover such proceeds. Customer shall provide reasonable proof of recovery; Redwood shall not be required to pursue claims on Customer's behalf.

Operational notes: requiring proof of recovery avoids speculative offsets. We should avoid offsets that require Redwood to pay claims into subrogation or to be named as a party to the customer's claim. Also recommend a carveout that consequential/indirect damages remain disclaimed to the fullest extent permitted by law.

I'll prepare a tracked redline of the MSA + Order Form for Laura to send — suggest we propose the annualized option as our baseline and accept insurance offsets only with the "actually received" language.

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear ask and patience while we synced internally. Below is the position Redwood would like to propose to your procurement/legal team; we think it balances predictability for BrightWave with reasonable protection for Redwood.

1) Preferred anchor: Annualized fee-based cap — "Redwood's liability for direct damages will be limited to the greater of (a) fees paid by BrightWave to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) $250,000." This keeps exposure tied to recent usage and avoids large tail risk on short pilots.

2) Insurance offsets: We will permit reduction of Redwood's exposure by insurance proceeds that BrightWave actually recovers, net of the customer's deductible and reasonable costs to obtain recovery. BrightWave would provide reasonable evidence of collection (e.g., insurer settlement notice and remittance). Redwood is not asking to be named as a party to Customer's insurance claim or to pursue recovery on Customer's behalf.

3) Carveouts: The usual exceptions will remain — willful misconduct, gross negligence causing data breach, and IP indemnity. Consequential and indirect damages remain excluded to the fullest extent permitted by law.

Attached is a tracked redline of the MSA + Order Form with the draft language inserted and a certificate template for insurance confirmation. If that looks acceptable, happy to route to your counsel and set a short call next week to finalize.

Next steps: please confirm whether BrightWave prefers annualized or aggregate math by end of day Wednesday; otherwise we'll assume the annualized formulation above and prepare a DocuSign package.
